solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Item of tableware in broken state quietly put back

indicators.note: put back tells us to write the assembled pieces in reverse order

parts.note: a broken horse has been tamed, so broken means tame
Cal is a short form of California, a US state
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone in a sorry condition quietly returns a piece of tableware to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' looks like describing the state; it means TAME. TAME + CAL + P, put back, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A place mat is a small table covering set under one diner's plate, so it is a piece of tableware.

clue.text: Three pounds secures ring, I report — that's sweet

indicators.note: secures means holds fast, so the pounds hold the ring within them

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), three times
O is ring-shaped
a report is a bang, a pop

explanation.surface: Someone pays three pounds for a ring and reports on it, finding it sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secures' puts O inside the three Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a boiled sweet on a stick, so it is something sweet.

clue.text: Give firm assurance, investing millions

indicators.note: investing literally means clothing or wrapping, so the firm and assurance wrap round the letter for millions

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a promise is an assurance
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A business gives a firm guarantee while putting millions into a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give' is a noun here, flexibility; 'investing' wraps the firm and the assurance round M.
explanation.definitionFit: Give, as a noun, is flexibility or yielding, which is what a compromise involves.

clue.text: One flyer in drink, another being on rescue vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, being on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: mead is an alcoholic drink made from honey
another flyer, a bird: owl
Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: One bird sits in a drink while another perches on a lifeboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is short for another flyer; 'being on' stacks it above the vessel in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadowlark is an American songbird, so it is one flying creature.

clue.text: Female chef, ultimately limited by time restriction, serves delicacy

indicators.note: limited by means hemmed in, so the time and restriction letters surround the others

parts.note: a rule is a restriction

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of chef

explanation.surface: A woman chef, working within strict time limits, serves up a delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited by' places F and F (the last letter of chef) inside T + RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A truffle is a prized underground fungus eaten as a luxury food.

clue.text: Sparkler hastily shortened at each end

indicators.note: shortened at each end means letters are cut from both the front and the back of the word

explanation.surface: A firework is hastily snipped at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened at each end' takes H from the front and LY from the back of hastily.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian white wine, so a sparkler.

clue.text: Touring lochs, picked up something from dog track

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece goes round the other
in a down clue picked up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: woof is the sound a dog makes
L stands for loch on maps, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone touring Scottish lochs picks up something a dog left on the trail.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog's something is its bark, not its mess; 'picked up' turns it upwards to FOOW, and 'Touring' wraps that round the lochs.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow is to track, as in trailing someone.

clue.text: Where it's unclear, agree to differ about chap that's upset

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the reversed name
to differ means to become different, so the letters are rearranged
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: Ray is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: Two people agree to differ about a man who is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to differ' rearranges agree as GREEA; 'that's upset' turns the chap round to YAR, which 'about' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a situation that is ambiguous, not clear-cut.

clue.text: Busy period requires routine with no time off, hospitals admitted

indicators.note: no tells us to leave out the time letter

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: milk that is off has gone sour
H is the abbreviation for hospital, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A busy spell demands routine without time off, with hospitals taking patients in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'time off'; it means SOUR. RU (RUT with no T) + SOUR takes in HH.
explanation.definitionFit: Rush hour is the peak commuting time, the busiest period on roads and trains.

clue.text: Agency, largely understanding manufacturing needs, arranges openings for graduate

indicators.note: openings are beginnings, so the first letter of each of these words is taken

parts.words: Agency, largely understanding manufacturing needs, arranges

explanation.surface: An agency with a grasp of manufacturing needs sets up job openings for a graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumna is a female former student, one who has graduated from a school or college.

clue.text: Uncertain about one religious group after daughter finds trouble

indicators.note: after means the rest follows the daughter letter
about means around, so the uncertain word goes round the others

parts.note: iffy is informal for uncertain
I is the Roman numeral one
a cult is a religious group

explanation.surface: A parent, unsure about a sect, discovers trouble once their daughter is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the uncertain word round one and the group; 'after' puts the daughter first.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficulty is a problem or a spot of trouble.

clue.text: Put another way, nothing doing

indicators.note: put another way means the letters are arranged differently

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: In other words, nothing is happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another way' rearranges PUT to UPT.
explanation.definitionFit: What are you up to? asks what you are doing, so up to means doing, engaged in.

clue.text: Fluid taken in by hippopotamus, say — one that's shy?

indicators.note: taken in by means enclosed, so the fluid letters sit inside

parts.note: a hippo wallows in mud, so it is an example of a wallower
fl is a short form of fluid, as in fl oz

explanation.surface: A hippo soaks up liquid; is it a timid creature?
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the hippo as an example of a WALLOWER, which takes in FL.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallflower is someone too timid to join in at a dance, hence a shy person; the question mark flags the plant pun.

clue.text: Worn-out fan belt bodged together with tie

indicators.note: bodged means botched or clumsily made, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A worn car fan belt has been badly fixed with a tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bodged' rearranges FAN BELT plus TIE. Bodged is British slang for a botched repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Flea-bitten means shabby and run-down, literally bitten by fleas.

clue.text: One carrying spare tyre may be finished with boat crew

definitions.text: One carrying spare tyre may be

parts.note: over means finished, done
a rowing eight is a boat crew

explanation.surface: A rower with a paunch might be finished with the rowing crew.
explanation.walkthrough: A spare tyre is a roll of fat at the waist, not a car spare.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone carrying a spare tyre round their middle is likely to weigh too much.

clue.text: Best man's embraced by old friend

indicators.note: embraced by means held within, so the man's name sits inside

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Tim is a man's name; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: The best man is hugged by an old friend at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best man' reads as one phrase, but 'Best' alone is the definition; 'embraced by' puts the man inside the old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal means the most favourable or ideal, the best possible.

clue.text: Letting down front, crease fabric and squeeze once

indicators.note: letting down the front means the first letter is moved lower, to the end in this down entry

parts.note: a fold is a crease
lame is a fabric woven with metallic threads

explanation.surface: Letting the hem down at the front means pressing and squeezing the fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letting down front' moves F of FOLD to the end, giving OLDF. Squeeze is slang for a romantic partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeeze is a boyfriend or girlfriend; an old flame is a former one.

clue.text: Girl runs along with a bunch of keys

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
E, B, E, C, C and A are all musical keys, named by letters

explanation.surface: A girl dashes along carrying a jangling bunch of keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keys' are musical keys, each named by a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is a girl's name.

clue.text: It's usually broadcast after the match

definitions.text: It's usually broadcast after the match

parts.words: It's usually broadcast after the match
parts.note: broadcast means scattered rather than televised, and the match is a wedding, not a game

explanation.surface: Something normally televised once the game is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests football highlights; the match is a marriage and broadcast means thrown about.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper pieces are thrown over newlyweds after a wedding, a match between two people.

clue.text: He died, supported by Duke in real push forward

indicators.note: in a down clue supported by means placed above the next piece

parts.note: ob. (obiit) is Latin for he died

indicators.note: in means the duke letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: true means real

explanation.surface: A man died, held up by a duke in a genuine push forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He died' is the Latin obiit, a gravestone abbreviation; 'supported by' stacks it above the rest in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to thrust forward or push oneself in unwanted.

clue.text: Food's ready, with baker excited — bravo!

parts.note: done means ready, as cooked food is

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: B is bravo in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Dinner is ready and the baker is thrilled: well done!
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges BAKER to RKEBA. The 's after Food stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A doner kebab is a takeaway dish of sliced spit-roast meat in bread.

clue.text: Nut enters rising river — that's devotion for you

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so the nut letters sit inside
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Avon is an English river
en is a printing unit, half an em; nut is printers' slang for it

explanation.surface: A nut drops into a river that is rising; that's devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the river upwards to NOVA; 'enters' puts the printers' nut inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A novena is a Catholic devotion of prayers said over nine days.

clue.text: Go first in division after gaining three points

indicators.note: after gaining means the division letter comes after the points

parts.note: W, E and N are compass points: west, east, north

indicators.note: first in points to the opening letter of division

explanation.surface: A team goes top of the division after picking up three points.
explanation.walkthrough: The points are compass points, not league points.
explanation.definitionFit: To wend is to go, as in wending one's way.

clue.text: Meat product novel writers "luv"

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A novel in which writers address readers as 'luv'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges WRITERS plus LUV.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverwurst is a liver sausage, a processed meat product.

clue.text: After whiskey, John spins yarn

indicators.note: after means the reversed word follows the whiskey letter

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: spins means turns round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, a loo

explanation.surface: After a few whiskeys, John tells a tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man; it is a toilet, LOO, which 'spins' to OOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Wool is spun fibre, i.e. yarn; the clue plays on yarn as a story.

clue.text: Thing that is regularly what ballet dancers wear

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A garment that ballet dancers routinely wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet dancers wear close-fitting leg garments for practice and performance.

clue.text: Crew provided obsolete engine part, for example

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
if means provided, on condition that
old means obsolete, outdated

explanation.surface: A crew supplied an outdated engine part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' looks like a noun but is the verb MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifold is a pipe with several openings, such as an engine's exhaust or inlet.

clue.text: One German mug? On the contrary!

definitions.text: One German mug? On the contrary!

parts.note: ein is German for one
a stein is a German beer mug

explanation.surface: Is this one a German fool? Quite the reverse!
explanation.walkthrough: Mug suggests a fool; 'On the contrary' says the answer is the opposite, a genius. EIN is German for one, STEIN a German mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the German-born physicist, is the byword for genius, the opposite of a mug or fool.
